Cache Data Leakage Through Misconfigured ElastiCache Security Groups [Information Disclosure, CWE-732] on ElastiCache-Primary, ElastiCache-Secondary, SecurityGroups: Overly permissive security group rules could allow unauthorized EC2 instances or external actors to connect to ElastiCache clusters. An attacker who compromises an EC2 instance in one VPC might be able to access ElastiCache clusters in another VPC or region if security groups are not properly configured.

Cache Poisoning via CloudFront [Tampering, Denial of Service, CWE-444] on CloudFront, Route53, ApplicationLoadBalancer: Attackers could potentially inject malicious content into the CloudFront cache by exploiting cache key manipulation or response header manipulation. An attacker could manipulate cache keys or headers to cause CloudFront to cache and serve malicious content to subsequent users requesting the same resource.

Race Conditions in Cache Rollback Operations [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-362] on RollbackHandlerLambda, ElastiCache-Primary, ElastiCache-Secondary, DynamoDB: Concurrent rollback operations across regions could lead to inconsistent cache states if proper synchronization mechanisms are not in place. During a rollback operation, simultaneous updates to cache clusters in different regions could result in data inconsistency or loss.

DNS-Based Cache Overload [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on Route53, ElastiCache-Primary, ElastiCache-Secondary: Attackers could exploit DNS misconfigurations to direct excessive traffic to cache clusters, potentially overwhelming them. An attacker could manipulate DNS queries to flood cache clusters with requests, causing service degradation.

Insecure TLS Configuration in Load Balancers [Information Disclosure, CWE-326] on ApplicationLoadBalancer, EC2-AppServers: Weak TLS configurations or outdated protocols could allow attackers to intercept or modify traffic between clients and application servers. An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit weak TLS configurations to intercept sensitive data.

Cross-Region Data Leakage [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-200] on ElastiCache-Primary, ElastiCache-Secondary, TransitGateway, DynamoDB: Insufficient isolation between regions could allow data to leak across regional boundaries or enable unauthorized access to cache data from different regions. An attacker who compromises one region's resources could potentially access or modify cache data in other regions due to improper isolation.
